fields.narrative_intro: *A blustering person and a slumped person discuss Goldman's Claude Code rollback on a malfunctioning space station.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
BLUSTERING PERSON: "After six months, Anthropic engineers lived here, installing Claude Code."
SLUMPED PERSON: "Goldman says everyone can vibe-code now."
fields.panel2:
[build]
BLUSTERING PERSON: "Goldman's CIO praised nontechnical employees' 'vibe coding' in July."
SLUMPED PERSON: "I just coded a trading strategy with interpretive dance."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
SLUMPED PERSON: "Update: Claude Code is restricted to 12,000 engineers."
BLUSTERING PERSON: "Among 47,000 staff, that's called 'determining the best use cases.'"
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: A blast door seals 35,000 bankers and traders outside; 12,000 engineers float inside with Claude Code.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
SLUMPED PERSON: "So the best use case is fewer users before ANT's November IPO?"
BLUSTERING PERSON: "We call that a 74-percent vibe correction."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: A tiny Claude Code shuttle departs toward a glowing ANT IPO ticker while 35,000 crew wave from the airlock.]

narrative_summary: Goldman's six-month Claude Code rollout blasts from July's vibe-coding hype to a 12,000-engineer airlock before Anthropic's ANT IPO.
rationale: Candidate 3 turns the exact 35,000-of-47,000 exclusion into the sharper, less predictable phrase “74-percent vibe correction,” while the airlock escalation gives the six-panel structure a clear visual and narrative payoff. The other candidates lean more heavily on the familiar corporate “best use cases” joke.
story_title: Goldman Sachs is pulling Claude Code from its bankers and traders
hat_pair: foam fishbowl helmet with a single plastic goldfish inside
firefighter helmet with a tiny rubber chicken mounted on top
